project.name: Online Examination Platform
project.summary: Web system for creating exams, delivering timed tests to students, and providing auto‑graded results.

functional_requirements: Teachers can create, edit, and delete question banks.
Teachers can schedule exams with start time, duration, and assigned student groups.
Students can take timed exams online.
The system automatically grades objective questions and stores results.
Teachers and students can view exam results on a dashboard.
non_functional_requirements: The platform must prevent cheating through question randomization and session monitoring.
The system must remain available and reliable throughout the entire exam window.
User interfaces must respond within 2 seconds for all interactive actions.
The application must scale to support concurrent exams for up to 5,000 students.

actors.name: Teacher
actors.description: Creates question banks, schedules exams, and reviews results.

actors.name: Student
actors.description: Logs in, takes assigned timed exams, and views personal results.

actors.name: Administrator
actors.description: Manages user accounts, roles, and global exam settings.

use_cases.name: Create Question Bank
use_cases.description: Teacher adds, edits, or deletes questions in a bank.

use_cases.name: Schedule Exam
use_cases.description: Teacher defines exam date, time, duration, and selects question bank.

use_cases.name: Take Exam
use_cases.description: Student starts the exam, answers questions within the time limit, and submits.

use_cases.name: Review Exam Results
use_cases.description: Teacher accesses auto‑graded results and analytics for each exam.

use_cases.name: Manage Users and Settings
use_cases.description: Administrator creates, updates, or removes user accounts and configures system parameters.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Teachers can create, edit, and delete question banks.
criteria: All question types can be added, modified, and removed without errors.
Changes are persisted and immediately available for exam scheduling.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Teachers can schedule exams with start time, duration, and assigned student groups.
criteria: Exam appears in the assigned students' dashboards at the scheduled time.
Scheduling conflicts are detected and prevented.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Students can take timed exams online.
criteria: A visible countdown timer starts when the exam begins.
Submission is blocked after the timer expires.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: The system automatically grades objective questions and stores results.
criteria: Grades are calculated instantly after submission.
Results are saved and retrievable from the dashboard.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: The platform must prevent cheating through question randomization and session monitoring.
criteria: Question order is randomized for each student session.
Multiple concurrent logins from the same account are detected and blocked.

user_stories.story: As a teacher, I want to create and organize question banks, so that I can reuse questions for multiple exams.
acceptance_criteria: Teachers can add, edit, and delete questions within a bank.
Questions are searchable and can be grouped by subject or difficulty.

user_stories.story: As a teacher, I want to schedule exams, so that students know when to take them.
acceptance_criteria: Teachers can set exam date, start time, duration, and associate a question bank.
Scheduled exams appear on the student dashboard with countdown timer.

user_stories.story: As a student, I want to take a timed test, so that I can complete assessments within the allocated period.
acceptance_criteria: The test starts automatically at the scheduled time and enforces the configured duration.
The interface disables navigation away from the exam page and records answers in real time.

user_stories.story: As a student, I want to view my results after the exam, so that I can understand my performance.
acceptance_criteria: Results display total score, per-question feedback, and overall percentile.
Results are accessible only to the student and authorized teachers.

user_stories.story: As an administrator, I want to manage users and exam settings, so that the platform remains organized and secure.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can create, edit, deactivate, and assign roles to user accounts.
Admins can configure global exam parameters such as time limits and password policies.

user_stories.story: As a system, I need to enforce anti‑cheating measures, so that exam integrity is maintained.
acceptance_criteria: The platform detects multiple simultaneous logins for the same account and blocks them.
During exams, screen capture, copy‑paste, and navigation away from the test window are prevented.

Database Designer.sql:
CREATE TABLE Users (
    user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    email TEXT,
    role TEXT,
    is_active BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE Exams (
    exam_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    title TEXT,
    scheduled_start DATETIME,
    duration_minutes INTEGER,
    creator_id INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (creator_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Questions (
    question_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    exam_id INTEGER,
    content TEXT,
    max_score REAL,
    question_type TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (exam_id) REFERENCES Exams(exam_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Attempts (
    attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    exam_id INTEGER,
    student_id INTEGER,
    start_time DATETIME,
    end_time DATETIME,
    score REAL,
    FOREIGN KEY (exam_id) REFERENCES Exams(exam_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

Project Structure.architecture: Microservice‑style monolith: a FastAPI backend serves REST and WebSocket endpoints, a React/Vite SPA consumes them, PostgreSQL stores users, exams, questions and results, Redis handles session caching and real‑time exam timers, Celery workers process auto‑grading, Nginx terminates TLS and proxies to backend containers. Docker Compose orchestrates services for development and production.
Project Structure.architecture_diagram:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Client
        UI[React SPA]
    end
    subgraph Server
        API[FastAPI REST]
        WS[FastAPI WebSocket]
        GR[Celery Worker]
        DB[(PostgreSQL)]
        Cache[(Redis)]
    end
    subgraph Infra
        Nginx[NGINX]
        Docker[Docker Compose]
    end
    UI -->|HTTPS| Nginx
    Nginx --> API
    Nginx --> WS
    API --> DB
    API --> Cache
    WS --> Cache
    GR --> DB
    GR --> Cache
    Docker --> Nginx
    Docker --> API
    Docker --> WS
    Docker --> GR

Documentation.readme: Online Exam Platform enables teachers to build question banks, schedule timed exams, and auto‑grade. Students log in, take exams within a secure, proctored environment, and view results instantly. Admins manage users, roles, and system settings. Built with React frontend, Node.js/Express API, PostgreSQL, and JWT authentication.
Documentation.api_documentation: POST /api/auth/login – body {email, password}. Returns JWT. GET /api/exams/:id – fetch exam details (auth, role: student). POST /api/exams/:id/submit – submit answers, returns score. GET /api/teachers/banks – list question banks. POST /api/teachers/banks – create bank. POST /api/admin/users – create user. All endpoints require Bearer token, role‑based access.
Documentation.installation: Clone repo. Run `npm install` in root. Set up PostgreSQL DB and create .env with DB_URL, JWT_SECRET. Run `npm run migrate` to apply schema. Start backend with `npm start`. In /client, run `npm install` then `npm run build`.
Documentation.deployment: Containerize with Docker. Use docker-compose with services: api, db, client. Deploy to cloud (AWS ECS, Azure App Service) behind HTTPS load balancer. Enable autoscaling for API pods. Use environment variables for secrets. Configure CI/CD pipeline to build and push images on merge.
Documentation.sprint_plan: Sprint 1 (2w): Auth, user roles, DB schema. Sprint 2 (2w): Question bank CRUD, exam scheduling UI. Sprint 3 (2w): Exam taking flow, timer, auto‑grade engine. Sprint 4 (2w): Admin dashboard, user management, settings. Sprint 5 (1w): Cheating mitigation (browser lockdown, IP monitoring). Sprint 6 (1w): QA, load testing, documentation.
Documentation.architecture: Frontend: React SPA with Redux, React Router, Material UI. Backend: Node.js/Express REST API, JWT auth, role middleware. Database: PostgreSQL relational schema for users, exams, questions, results. Security: HTTPS, CSP, SameSite cookies, server‑side validation, exam session tokens, activity logging. Scalability: Stateless API, load‑balanced containers, DB read replicas.
